name: btrfs_subpage_test_##name
prose: Generated by IMPLEMENT_BTRFS_SUBPAGE_TEST_OP(uptodate) as btrfs_subpage_test_uptodate(fs_info, folio, start, len). Precondition: folio is a subpage folio with a btrfs_folio_state in its private pointer, start and len are sector aligned and the range [start, start + len) lies inside the folio. Postcondition: with bfs->lock held (irq-saving) it returns true iff every bit of the uptodate sub-bitmap of the folio covering the range (len >> sectorsize_bits bits starting at the bit computed by subpage_calc_start_bit) is set (bitmap_test_range_all_set), false if any is clear; it modifies nothing and releases the lock before returning. The same generator produces the dirty, writeback, ordered and checked variants.

name: btrfs_folio_test_##name
prose: Generated by IMPLEMENT_BTRFS_PAGE_OPS(uptodate, ...) as btrfs_folio_test_uptodate(fs_info, folio, start, len). Precondition: folio is a valid locked or referenced folio; for a subpage folio its private state is a btrfs_folio_state and the range [start, start + len) is sector aligned inside the folio. Postcondition: if fs_info is NULL (selftests) or the folio is not a subpage folio, it returns folio_test_uptodate(folio), ignoring start and len; otherwise it returns btrfs_subpage_test_uptodate(fs_info, folio, start, len), i.e. true iff all uptodate bits of the range are set. It modifies nothing and takes no lock beyond the one inside the subpage helper.

name: btrfs_set_free_space_cache_settings
prose: Precondition: fs_info is a btrfs_fs_info during open_ctree() whose mount options are already populated from the mount parameters, with a readable super_copy; the function returns nothing. Postcondition: if sectorsize < PAGE_SIZE and the SPACE_CACHE option is set, an info message is logged, SPACE_CACHE is cleared and FREE_SPACE_TREE is set, and execution continues. Then, if the FREE_SPACE_TREE option is set (including just now) it returns. Else if the filesystem is zoned and the v1 free space cache is active it logs a message, sets the superblock cache generation to 0 and returns without changing any option. Else if SPACE_CACHE or NOSPACECACHE is set it returns unchanged. Otherwise it sets the FREE_SPACE_TREE option when the FREE_SPACE_TREE compat_ro feature is on disk, else sets SPACE_CACHE when the v1 free space cache is active, else changes nothing. No lock, reference or memory is acquired.

name: btrfs_get_subvol_name_from_objectid
prose: Precondition: fs_info is a mounted btrfs filesystem, subvol_objectid is a subvolume id; the caller owns the result and must kfree it when it is not an error pointer. Postcondition: returns a kmalloc'ed NUL-terminated string of at most PATH_MAX bytes holding the path of the subvolume relative to the top-level subvolume, built by walking from subvol_objectid upwards: for each step it takes the ROOT_BACKREF of the subvolume (giving its parent subvolume and name), prepends '/' and that name, then walks the directory chain of the parent subvolume with INODE_REF items prepending '/' and each directory name until the subvolume root directory is reached, and stops when the parent is BTRFS_FS_TREE_OBJECTID; for the top-level subvolume itself the string is "/". It returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if the path or the name buffer cannot be allocated, ERR_PTR(-ENOENT) if a backref or inode ref is missing, ERR_PTR(-ENAMETOOLONG) if the path would not fit in PATH_MAX, and ERR_PTR of the negative errno of btrfs_search_backwards or btrfs_get_fs_root otherwise. In all cases the btrfs path is freed and any root reference obtained is put; on failure the name buffer is freed too.

name: simple_test
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid transaction handle (with initialised delayed refs), head_check and node_check describe the expected delayed ref head and the expected delayed ref node for one reference, node_check->type selecting a metadata (tree block ref or shared block ref type) or data reference. Postcondition: builds a btrfs_ref from node_check (nodesize bytes) and adds it with btrfs_add_delayed_tree_ref or btrfs_add_delayed_data_ref; if that fails it logs and returns the error without selecting a head and without destroying delayed refs. It then selects a ref head: if none can be selected it logs and returns -EINVAL, again without unselecting or destroying anything. Otherwise the result starts as -EINVAL; it is 0 only if the head matches head_check (bytenr, num_bytes, ref_mod, total_ref_mod, must_insert_reserved), a delayed ref node can be selected from the head and the node matches node_check (bytenr, num_bytes, ref_mod, action, parent, root, type, owner, offset). On every path after a head was selected the head is unselected and all delayed refs of the transaction are destroyed (btrfs_destroy_delayed_refs) before returning 0 or -EINVAL.

name: merge_tests
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid transaction handle with a fake extent-tree environment and type is BTRFS_REF_METADATA or BTRFS_REF_DATA; the function is a selftest (its name is not in the slice, it is the function containing the slice). Postcondition: it adds delayed refs to the same bytenr in several scenarios (add then drop; two adds; two drops; ten adds then twelve drops; ten drops then twelve adds; fifty adds and fifty drops with various roots and parents) and after each checks, with validate_ref_head and validate_ref_node, that the selected head has the expected ref_mod and total_ref_mod, that the remaining node (if any) has the expected action and count, and that no node remains when the refs cancel out; each checked head and node is deleted again before the next scenario. It returns 0 when all checks pass and -EINVAL when a validation fails or a node is unexpectedly missing or present, or the negative errno of a failing btrfs_add_delayed_tree_ref or btrfs_add_delayed_data_ref. When the ref head cannot be selected in the first three scenarios the failure is only logged and the function returns 0 because ret is not set there, while in the later scenarios it returns -EINVAL. On every path the currently selected head, if any, is unselected and all delayed refs of the transaction are destroyed (btrfs_destroy_delayed_refs).

name: test_steal_space_from_bitmap_to_extent
prose: Precondition: cache is a btrfs_block_group with an empty free space cache and sectorsize is the filesystem sector size; the function is a selftest (its name is not in the slice, it is the function containing the slice). Postcondition: it replaces cache->free_space_ctl->op by a test op that forces bitmap use, then runs two scenarios (an extent entry to the left of a bitmap entry and one to the right) in which it adds and removes free space and checks, using check_num_extents_and_bitmaps, test_check_exists, free_space_ctl->free_space and btrfs_find_space_for_alloc, that free space is stolen from the bitmap into the extent entry (so that 1MiB can be allocated at the expected offset, then the remaining sectorsize or 2 * sectorsize from the bitmap) and that the cache ends empty. It returns 0 if everything matches, in which case the original free space op is restored and the cache is cleared with btrfs_remove_free_space_cache. It returns the negative errno of the first failing step (-ENOENT when an expected free region is missing, -EINVAL for an unexpected free region, a wrong free space total or a wrong allocation offset, or the error of test_add_free_space_entry, btrfs_add_free_space, btrfs_remove_free_space, check_num_extents_and_bitmaps or check_cache_empty); on those error returns the original free space op is not restored and the cache is not cleared.

name: test_btrfs_get_extent
prose: Precondition: sectorsize and nodesize are valid btrfs sector and node sizes; the function is a selftest (its name is not in the slice, it is the function containing the slice). Postcondition: it creates a test inode, dummy fs_info and root with an empty root node, checks that btrfs_get_extent on an empty tree returns a hole, builds a fixed file extent layout with setup_file_extents and then checks a sequence of extent maps (inline, regular, prealloc, compressed, split compressed, regular, hole between extents and the final regular extents) for the expected start, len, flags, offset, block start and compression type, freeing each extent map after use. It returns 0 if all extent maps match, -ENOMEM if the inode, fs_info, root or root node cannot be allocated, and -EINVAL if btrfs_get_extent returns an error or any check fails. On every path the last extent map is freed (if valid), the inode is iput and the dummy root and fs_info are freed.

name: btrfs_test_raid_stripe_tree
prose: Precondition: sectorsize and nodesize are the sector and node sizes used to build the dummy test filesystem; the function is a selftest driver. Postcondition: it runs each test of the static tests array (simple create/delete, create/update/delete, tail delete, front delete, front delete with previous item, punch hole, punch hole over three extents, delete of two extents) in order through run_test, which builds and frees its own dummy fs_info, root and devices for each test. It returns 0 if every test passes; on the first failure it logs the test name and error and returns that error without running the remaining tests. The error is -ENOMEM if the dummy fs_info allocation fails, the PTR_ERR of a failed dummy root, root node or dummy device allocation, or the value returned by the test function. This function itself allocates and frees nothing.

name: btrfs_write_marked_extents
prose: Precondition: fs_info is a valid filesystem with a btree inode, dirty_pages is an extent_io_tree and mark is the extent bit selecting the btree ranges to write; the caller keeps ownership of all arguments. Postcondition: for each range of dirty_pages that has the bit mark, found in ascending order, it converts the range from mark to EXTENT_NEED_WAIT and starts writeback of the range of the btree inode mapping with filemap_fdatawrite_range. If the conversion fails with -ENOMEM the error is ignored and, provided filemap_fdatawrite_range then succeeds, writeback of that range is also waited for (btrfs_btree_wait_writeback_range, no return value) because the NEED_WAIT bit could not be set. Any other conversion error, or an error from filemap_fdatawrite_range, stops the loop (the cached extent state of the current range is freed first) and is returned, so the remaining ranges are not written. Returns 0 when all ranges were converted and submitted, otherwise that first error. cond_resched is called between ranges; no lock or reference remains held.

name: create_pending_snapshot
prose: Precondition: trans is a running transaction handle in the commit phase, pending is an initialised pending-snapshot descriptor with non-NULL path and root_item, and root, dir, dentry and readonly describe the source subvolume, parent directory and new name. Postcondition: the function always clears the pending state before returning: new_root_item is freed and pending->root_item and pending->path are set to NULL (the path is freed), the filename is freed if it was set up, and the skip-qgroup mark is cleared once it was set. Early failures (fscrypt_setup_filename, btrfs_get_free_objectid, reservation of the relocation metadata with btrfs_block_rsv_add) store the errno in pending->error and return 0; an existing directory entry of the same name stores -EEXIST in pending->error and returns 0 after restoring trans->block_rsv and clearing trans->bytes_reserved. Otherwise it switches trans->block_rsv to the pending reservation and performs the snapshot: records the roots in the transaction, picks the directory index, checks that the name does not exist, creates the qgroup (an -ENOTCONN with quotas disabled is ignored), runs the delayed items, sets last_snapshot, copies the root item (readonly flag per pending->readonly, new uuid, parent uuid, otime), COWs and copies the root node, inserts the new root item, root ref and the new fs root (pending->snap), does the relocation and qgroup accounting, inserts the directory item, updates the parent inode and adds the subvolume uuid and, if present, the received uuid to the uuid tree (-EOVERFLOW is turned into 0, other errors except -EEXIST abort the transaction). On any failure after the reservation switch it sets pending->error to the errno and returns it; most failures also abort the transaction (qgroup accounting failures do not), and an -EEXIST from the received-uuid insertion is not abort-worthy but is still returned and stored in pending->error. On success it returns 0 and pending->error is 0. In all paths after the switch trans->block_rsv is restored and trans->bytes_reserved is cleared; pending->snap is not released here and stays set once btrfs_get_new_fs_root succeeded.

name: btrfs_commit_transaction
prose: Precondition: trans is the only user of its handle (use_count == 1) for the running transaction of trans->fs_info and the caller holds no transaction-related lock. Postcondition: in every case the caller's handle is consumed (ended through btrfs_end_transaction or freed), so the caller must not use trans afterwards, and a pending snapshot attached to trans is linked into the transaction's pending list (add_pending_snapshot, under trans_lock, once the state is at least COMMIT_PREP) so that the caller may safely free it if the commit returns an error. If the transaction is already aborted, or flushing the delayed refs or starting the dirty block groups fails, the function ends the handle and returns the abort error or that step's negative errno without cleaning up the transaction itself. If another task is already committing (state at least COMMIT_PREP) it ends its own handle, waits until the commit is COMPLETED (SUPER_COMMITTED for an fsync) and returns the transaction's abort error if it aborted, otherwise the result of btrfs_end_transaction. Otherwise this task performs the commit: it waits for the previous transaction (returning its abort error, or -EROFS if the filesystem is in an error state and no previous transaction exists), flushes delalloc and delayed items, waits for writers and ordered extents, pauses scrub, creates pending snapshots, runs the delayed refs, commits fs roots and cow-only roots, accounts qgroups, switches the commit roots and updates the superblock copy, then writes the btree pages and the superblocks and finishes the extent commit, moving the state through COMMIT_START, COMMIT_DOING, UNBLOCKED, SUPER_COMMITTED and COMPLETED, waking the waiters, setting the last committed transid, removing the transaction from the list, dropping both transaction references, freeing the handle and resuming scrub. It returns 0 on that success path. If any of those steps fails (including write errors, which are reported with btrfs_handle_fs_error) the transaction is cleaned up: metadata and pending block groups are released, the handle is detached from the task, a warning is logged and cleanup_transaction aborts the transaction with the error, removes and destroys it and frees the handle; the negative errno is returned.

name: btrfs_transaction_init
prose: Precondition: none; it is called once at module initialisation. Postcondition: it creates the slab cache for struct btrfs_trans_handle (SLAB_TEMPORARY) and stores it in the global btrfs_trans_handle_cachep. It returns 0 when the cache was created, and returns the negative value -12 (the out-of-memory error) when the cache could not be created, in which case btrfs_trans_handle_cachep is NULL; no other value is returned and no lock or reference is involved.

name: check_extent_item
prose: Precondition: leaf is a btrfs leaf, slot is the slot of an EXTENT_ITEM or METADATA_ITEM, key is that item's key and prev_key is the key of the previous item in the leaf; the function only reads. Postcondition: returns 0 when the item is well formed, and -EUCLEAN (after logging the first problem) when any of the following holds: a METADATA_ITEM key without the SKINNY_METADATA feature; key->objectid not sector aligned; a METADATA_ITEM whose level (key->offset) is >= BTRFS_MAX_LEVEL; item size smaller than struct btrfs_extent_item; extent generation greater than the superblock generation + 1; extent flags that do not have exactly one of DATA and TREE_BLOCK set; for a tree block with an EXTENT_ITEM key, key->offset != nodesize; for a data extent, a key type other than EXTENT_ITEM, an unaligned length, or the FULL_BACKREF flag set; a tree block info level >= BTRFS_MAX_LEVEL; an inline ref that overflows the item, has an unknown type, or has an invalid body (a shared block ref or shared data ref parent that is not sector aligned, a data ref with an invalid root, an objectid outside [BTRFS_FIRST_FREE_OBJECTID, BTRFS_LAST_FREE_OBJECTID], an unaligned offset or zero count, a shared data ref with zero count); inline refs out of order (types must be ascending and, within one type, the sequence number (offset, or the data ref hash) must be non-increasing); padding bytes after the last inline ref; the sum of inline ref counts exceeding the extent's total refs; or the previous EXTENT_ITEM/METADATA_ITEM ends beyond key->objectid (overlap). The extent buffer is not modified and no lock or reference is taken.

name: log_dir_items
prose: Precondition: trans is a running transaction handle, inode is a directory inode whose root has a log root, path and dst_path are unused scratch paths, ctx is the log context, min_offset is the first dir index offset to consider and last_offset_ret is a writable u64 pointer. Postcondition: searches the subvolume tree for DIR_INDEX keys of the directory changed in this transaction from min_offset on, logs every such item through process_dir_items_leaf (batched), and records the range that the log covers by inserting one DIR_LOG_INDEX range key with insert_dir_log_key when last_old_dentry_offset + 1 <= last_offset. If nothing from this transaction is found, the covered range starts after the last existing dir index key (or min_offset - 1 if none) and ends at (u64)-1. last_old_dentry_offset is the offset of the dir index key just before the first logged one (or min_offset - 1), and the end of the range last_offset is (u64)-1 when the scan reached the end of the directory's dir index keys, or the offset of the next key minus 1 when the scan stopped at a leaf not changed in this transaction. On return 0, *last_offset_ret is set to that last_offset (the end of the covered range, not one past the last logged key). The result is 0 on success (a positive result of process_dir_items_leaf, meaning the last item was found, is turned into 0), or a negative errno from btrfs_search_slot, btrfs_previous_item, btrfs_next_item, btrfs_next_leaf, process_dir_items_leaf or insert_dir_log_key, in which case *last_offset_ret is not written. Both path and dst_path are released on all paths except when the fallback btrfs_search_slot (nothing found for this transaction) fails, where only path is released before returning the error.

name: btrfs_recover_log_trees
prose: Precondition: called during mount with log_root_tree the log root tree of the filesystem, on a filesystem being mounted read-write, with no other log replay in progress. Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM at once if the path cannot be allocated. Otherwise it sets BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING, starts a transaction on the tree root (a failure is returned after cleanup), pins all blocks of the log root tree, and then walks all log roots (TREE_LOG_OBJECTID root items, from the highest offset downward) in the stages pin, replay inodes, and replay everything: for each log root it reads the log tree and looks up the subvolume root with the same id; if the subvolume root does not exist (-ENOENT) the log's root block is pinned and the log is skipped; otherwise the log root is attached to the subvolume root, the root is recorded in the transaction, the log tree is walked, and in the final stage the inode link counts are fixed up and the root's free objectid is re-initialised. Temporary root references (the log root and the subvolume root) are dropped for each log. After the last stage the path is freed, the transaction is committed (which unpins the blocks) and, if the commit succeeded, BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING is cleared and 0 is returned; if the commit fails its error is returned and the flag stays set. On any error before the commit (walk_log_tree, btrfs_search_slot, btrfs_read_tree_root, btrfs_get_fs_root other than -ENOENT, btrfs_pin_extent_for_log_replay, btrfs_record_root_in_trans, fixup_inode_link_counts, btrfs_init_root_free_objectid) the transaction is aborted (not when starting it failed), the transaction handle is ended if one was started, the log root reference is put, BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING is cleared, the path is freed and the negative errno is returned.

name: replay_one_extent
prose: Precondition: wc->trans is a running transaction, wc->root is the subvolume root being replayed with a log root, wc->log_leaf, wc->log_slot and wc->log_key identify an EXTENT_DATA item in the log tree, and wc->subvol_path is released on entry. Postcondition: for an extent type other than REG, PREALLOC or INLINE it aborts the log replay and returns -EUCLEAN; if the inode cannot be read (btrfs_iget_logging) it aborts the replay and returns that error. Otherwise, if the subvolume already has an identical REG/PREALLOC file extent item at the same offset, it does nothing more and returns 0. Else it drops the extents overlapping [start, extent_end) (extent_end = start + num_bytes, or the sector-aligned end for an inline extent) with btrfs_drop_extents; an inline extent is then overwritten with overwrite_item; a hole with the NO_HOLES feature is only accounted; for other items the file extent item is inserted into the subvolume tree, an explicit hole needs nothing more, and a real extent is qgroup-traced, then either referenced (btrfs_inc_extent_ref) if it already exists in the extent tree or allocated (btrfs_alloc_logged_file_extent) if not, and the checksums covering it are read from the log root, the existing checksums of that range are deleted from the csum tree and the logged ones added. Finally the file extent range [start, extent_end) is recorded in the inode, the inode byte count is updated by the extent size and the dropped bytes, and the inode item is updated. It returns 0 on success, or the negative errno of the failing step, each of which also aborts the log replay with a message. The inode reference taken is dropped (iput) on every return after it was obtained, and the temporary checksum list is freed.

name: btrfs_get_old_root
prose: Precondition: root is a btrfs root with a tree modification log and time_seq is a sequence number registered with that log; the caller must call btrfs_tree_read_unlock and free_extent_buffer on a non-NULL result. Postcondition: it read-locks the current root node; if the log has no root modification at or after time_seq it returns that very root node (still read-locked, with the caller owning the reference). Otherwise it releases the read lock and reference on the current root node and builds a copy of the root as it was at time_seq: when the oldest relevant operation was a root replace and the old root block still has log entries, it reads the old root block from disk (a failed or not up-to-date read is logged and results in NULL), clones it, looks the log up again and returns NULL if the later entry is missing or older; when the old root has no usable log entries it allocates a dummy extent buffer at the old root's logical address; when there was no root replace it clones the current root node. It returns NULL if any clone or allocation fails. For a replaced root the header (bytenr, backref revision, owner, level, generation) is set to the old root values. The returned buffer is read-locked and has all the log operations after time_seq rewound (tree_mod_log_rewind). On every path the read lock and reference of the temporary buffers (the current root node when not returned, the old block, and eb on failure) are released.

name: btrfs_bg_flags_to_raid_index
prose: Precondition: none, flags is any u64 block group flags value. Postcondition: let profile = flags & BTRFS_BLOCK_GROUP_PROFILE_MASK (bits 3 to 10: RAID0, RAID1, DUP, RAID10, RAID5, RAID6, RAID1C3, RAID1C4). If profile is 0 the result is BTRFS_RAID_SINGLE (0). Otherwise the result is ilog2(profile >> 2), that is the position of the highest set profile bit minus 2: RAID0 gives 1, RAID1 2, DUP 3, RAID10 4, RAID5 5, RAID6 6, RAID1C3 7 and RAID1C4 8 when exactly one profile bit is set, and when several profile bits are set the highest bit decides. The result is always in [0, 8], below BTRFS_NR_RAID_TYPES (9). It is a pure function with no lock, reference or memory effect.

name: btrfs_nr_parity_stripes
prose: Precondition: none, type is any u64 block group type value. Postcondition: the result is the nparity field of btrfs_raid_array for the raid type selected by btrfs_bg_flags_to_raid_index(type), which looks at the highest set profile bit of type (bits 3 to 10): 1 if that highest profile bit is the RAID5 bit, 2 if it is the RAID6 bit, and 0 in every other case (no profile bit, or a highest profile bit of RAID0, RAID1, DUP, RAID10, RAID1C3 or RAID1C4). In particular RAID5 together with RAID6 gives 2, and RAID5 together with RAID1C3 gives 0. It is a pure lookup with no lock, reference or memory effect.

name: find_free_dev_extent
prose: Precondition: device is a valid btrfs_device whose fs_info has a dev_root, num_bytes is the requested hole length (a multiple of the zone size if the device is zoned), start points to a writable u64 and len is NULL or points to a writable u64. Postcondition: it searches the commit root of the device tree, without locking, for the free hole of at least num_bytes bytes inside the device range [search_start, total_bytes) where search_start comes from dev_extent_search_start(device). On every return, including error returns, *start is set to the start of the largest hole found (initially search_start) and, if len is non-NULL, *len to its size (initially 0). It returns -ENOMEM if the path cannot be allocated, -ENOSPC without searching if search_start >= total_bytes or the device is a replace target, the negative errno of btrfs_search_backwards or btrfs_next_leaf on a search error, 0 as soon as a hole of at least num_bytes is found between two device extents (after dev_extent_hole_check has adjusted the hole for alignment or zones), and otherwise, after examining the trailing space up to total_bytes, 0 if the largest hole is at least num_bytes and -ENOSPC if not. The reported hole never extends past the end of the device. The path is freed on every return.

name: btrfs_init_new_device
prose: Precondition: fs_info is a mounted btrfs filesystem, device_path names a block device to add, and the caller already holds the exclusive device-add operation. Postcondition: returns -EROFS if the filesystem is read-only and not a seeding one, the error of bdev_file_open_by_path (opening the device for write), -EINVAL if the device zone type does not match or the device is not larger than BTRFS_DEVICE_RANGE_RESERVED, -EEXIST if the device is already part of the filesystem, and the error of btrfs_alloc_device, lookup_bdev, btrfs_get_dev_zone_info, starting the transaction, btrfs_init_sprout, init_first_rw_device, btrfs_add_dev_item or btrfs_finish_sprout. For a seeding filesystem it takes s_umount for writing and uuid_mutex for the duration of the operation. On the success path the new writeable device is added to the device lists and counters (num_devices, open_devices, rw_devices, total_devices, total_rw_bytes), free_chunk_space is increased, the superblock total bytes and device count are updated, the sysfs entry and the dev item are added, the full flags of the space infos are cleared and the transaction is committed; for a seeding filesystem it also sprouts it, releases the locks, relocates the system chunks and commits again. After a successful setup it forgets scanned alien devices and updates the device time, and returns the result of the commit (0 on success; a failed first commit in the seeding case is returned right after unlocking, without rollback). On every failure before the commit the added device is removed again (sysfs entry, list entries, counters and the superblock totals are restored), the transaction is ended, the zone info is destroyed, the device is freed, the block device reference is dropped with bdev_fput and, if still held, uuid_mutex and s_umount are released.

name: btrfs_resume_balance_async
prose: Precondition: fs_info is a mounted btrfs filesystem during mount or remount read-write; when a paused balance is to be resumed, fs_info->exclusive_operation is BTRFS_EXCLOP_BALANCE_PAUSED (asserted). Postcondition: returns 0 without changing anything if fs_info->balance_ctl is NULL (checked under balance_mutex), and returns 0 after logging that the resume was skipped, again without changing the exclusive operation or the balance flags, if the SKIP_BALANCE mount option is set. Otherwise it sets fs_info->exclusive_operation to BTRFS_EXCLOP_BALANCE under super_lock, sets BTRFS_BALANCE_RESUME in balance_ctl->flags under balance_lock, and starts the kernel thread "btrfs-balance" running balance_kthread, returning 0 if the thread was created or the negative errno from kthread_run otherwise (in which case the exclusive operation and the flag have nevertheless been changed). It does not wait for the balance to finish, and keeps no lock.

name: btrfs_device_get_##name
prose: Generated by BTRFS_DEVICE_GETSET_FUNCS(name) as btrfs_device_get_<name>(dev) for a u64 field of struct btrfs_device (for example total_bytes, disk_total_bytes, bytes_used). Precondition: dev is a valid btrfs_device. Postcondition: returns the current value of dev->name as a u64 and modifies nothing. On a 32-bit SMP build it loops reading dev->data_seqcount until no writer interfered, so the value is never torn; on a 32-bit preemptible build it reads the field with preemption disabled; on other builds it is a plain read. No lock or reference is taken or kept.

name: btrfs_device_set_##name
prose: Generated by BTRFS_DEVICE_GETSET_FUNCS(name) as btrfs_device_set_<name>(dev, size) for a u64 field of struct btrfs_device. Precondition: dev is a valid btrfs_device and the caller serialises concurrent writers of the field (no lock is taken here). Postcondition: dev->name equals size and nothing else changes; returns nothing. On a 32-bit SMP build the store is done with preemption disabled inside a write_seqcount_begin/end pair on dev->data_seqcount so readers retry instead of seeing a torn value; on a 32-bit preemptible build the store is done with preemption disabled; on other builds it is a plain store. Preemption is re-enabled before returning.

name: sb_write_pointer
prose: Precondition: bdev is the block device, zones points to the two (BTRFS_NR_SB_LOG_ZONES) superblock log zone descriptors of one mirror, neither of which is a conventional zone (asserted), and wp_ret points to a writable u64. Postcondition: if both zones are empty it sets *wp_ret to the byte address of the start of zones[0] and returns -ENOENT (no superblock written yet). If both zones are full it reads the last superblock slot of each zone through the block device page cache (the invalidate lock is held only around each read; an error from read_cache_page_gfp is returned, after releasing the first superblock page if the second read failed, and *wp_ret is not written) and sets *wp_ret to the byte address of the start of zones[1] if the generation of the superblock in zones[0] is greater than that in zones[1], otherwise of zones[0], then releases both superblock pages and returns 0. If zone 0 is not full and zone 1 is empty or full, *wp_ret is the byte address of the write pointer of zones[0] and 0 is returned; if zone 0 is full (and zone 1 neither empty nor full) it is the write pointer of zones[1] and 0 is returned. In every other state (both partially written, or zone 0 empty and zone 1 partially written) it returns -EUCLEAN without writing *wp_ret. No reference or lock stays held.

name: btrfs_find_allocatable_zones
prose: Precondition: device is a zoned device with a non-NULL zone_info, hole_start and num_bytes are multiples of the zone size (asserted) and hole_start <= hole_end. Postcondition: returns a zone-aligned device position pos; it takes no lock and acquires no reference. Starting at hole_start while pos < hole_end it considers the region [pos, pos + num_bytes). If the region would end beyond the last zone of the device the function returns hole_end. If the zone at pos is sequential and the nzones zones of the region are not all marked empty, pos advances by one zone and the search continues (when the zone at pos is conventional the emptiness of the following zones is not checked). If the region overlaps the zones used by a superblock log (for each of the superblock mirrors) pos moves to the first zone after that log, and if it overlaps the byte range of a regular superblock copy pos moves to the zone-aligned position after that copy; the search then continues. If none of these happen the loop stops and pos is returned. The result is therefore either hole_end (device too small), or the first candidate position that satisfies the conditions, or a position reached by the last advance, which can be at or beyond hole_end when no suitable region exists inside the hole (the caller must compare the result against hole_end).

name: btrfs_zone_activate
prose: Precondition: block_group is a btrfs block group of the filesystem and the caller holds neither fs_info->zone_active_bgs_lock nor block_group->lock. Postcondition: returns true at once, with no lock taken, if the filesystem is not zoned. Otherwise it takes zone_active_bgs_lock and block_group->lock and returns true (releasing both) if the ZONE_IS_ACTIVE flag is already set. For a data block group that is full it warns and returns false. Otherwise, for each stripe of the block group's physical map whose device has a block device and a non-zero max_active_zones: if the device's active_zones_left is not above the reserved zones (the device's reserved_active_zones for data block groups, 0 for others) it returns false, and if the zone of the stripe cannot be activated (btrfs_dev_set_active_zone fails) it returns false; for a non-data block group it decrements the device's reserved_active_zones after each successful stripe. On failure the zones activated and reservations decremented for earlier stripes are not undone, no reference is taken and the block group is not added to the active list. When all stripes succeed it sets BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_ZONE_IS_ACTIVE, takes a block group reference (held while the group stays on the list), appends the block group to fs_info->zone_active_bgs and returns true. Both locks are released on every return.

name: btrfs_check_active_zone_reservation
prose: Precondition: fs_info is a btrfs filesystem in the mount context (no concurrent change of avail_metadata_alloc_bits or avail_system_alloc_bits); the function returns nothing. Postcondition: returns without any effect if BTRFS_FS_ACTIVE_ZONE_TRACKING is not set. Otherwise it computes metadata_reserve = 2 (4 if the available metadata allocation bits include DUP) and system_reserve = 1 (2 if the available system allocation bits include DUP); under device_list_mutex it sets zone_info->reserved_active_zones = metadata_reserve + system_reserve for every device that has a block device (devices without one are skipped); and under zone_active_bgs_lock, for every active block group whose flags include METADATA or SYSTEM, it decrements reserved_active_zones once for each stripe of the block group's physical map on that stripe's device (so the reservation is released for zones already in use). Both locks are released before returning.

name: btrfs_get_dev_zone_info
prose: Precondition: device is a btrfs_device with fs_info and bdev set, and populate_cache says whether to allocate the zone cache (used only for a real zoned device). Postcondition: returns 0 without change if the ZONED incompat feature is off or device->zone_info is already set. Otherwise it allocates device->zone_info (-ENOMEM on failure), determines the zone size (the emulated zone size of the filesystem for a non-zoned device, else the device's zone size) and returns -EINVAL if it is larger than BTRFS_MAX_ZONE_SIZE or smaller than BTRFS_MIN_ZONE_SIZE, computes the number of zones, queries max active zones, allocates the sequential, empty and active zone bitmaps, a zone report buffer and, when requested for a zoned bdev, the zone cache (-ENOMEM on any failure), and reads the zone report for the whole device filling the bitmaps and counting zones that are open or closed; it returns -EIO if the number of reported zones differs from nr_zones. If the active zone count exceeds max_active_zones it returns -EIO when the block device reports a positive active zone limit and otherwise sets max_active_zones to 0 (old filesystems); if not, it sets active_zones_left to the remaining count and sets BTRFS_FS_ACTIVE_ZONE_TRACKING. It then validates the superblock log zones of each mirror that lies inside the device: -EUCLEAN if two zones cannot be read or sb_write_pointer reports anything other than success or -ENOENT (mirrors whose first zone is conventional are skipped), or the errno of btrfs_get_dev_zones. On success it frees the report buffer, logs the zone model and returns 0. On every failure the report buffer is freed and device->zone_info is destroyed (bitmaps, cache and structure freed, pointer set to NULL) and the errno is returned.

name: btrfs_check_zoned_mode
prose: Precondition: fs_info is a btrfs filesystem during mount whose device list is populated and, when the ZONED incompat feature is set, every device with a block device already has zone_info. Postcondition: if ZONED is not set it modifies nothing and returns 0, or -EINVAL (after an error message) if any device with a block device is a zoned device. If ZONED is set it first resets fs_info->limits to stacking limits (this is kept even on error returns), takes the zone size of the first device that has a block device (devices without a bdev are skipped), returns -EINVAL if another such device has a different zone size, stacks the queue limits of the zoned devices, and returns the error of blk_validate_limits if the limits are invalid. It returns -EINVAL if the zone size (0 when no device has a bdev) is not aligned to BTRFS_STRIPE_LEN or if the MIXED_GROUPS feature is set. Otherwise it sets fs_info->zone_size, fs_info->max_zone_append_size (the minimum of the stacked append, sector and segment limits, aligned down to the sector size), the chunk allocation policy to BTRFS_CHUNK_ALLOC_ZONED and max_extent_size = min_not_zero(max_extent_size, max_zone_append_size), then checks the mount options for zoned mode (its error is returned, with the fields above already modified), logs that zoned mode is enabled and returns 0.

name: __block_write_full_folio
prose: Precondition: folio is locked, belongs to inode's mapping and is not under writeback (a BUG otherwise), get_block maps (and, with create set, may allocate) a file block into a buffer head, and wbc describes the writeback (sync_mode selects blocking or non-blocking buffer locking). Postcondition: buffers are created for the folio if needed. In a first pass, every buffer lying wholly beyond i_size is cleaned and marked uptodate, and every dirty buffer that is unmapped or delayed-allocated is mapped by get_block(inode, block, bh, 1) (clearing its delay flag and, if new, its new flag and any block device alias). In a second pass every mapped buffer is locked (with WB_SYNC_NONE only if trylock succeeds, otherwise the folio is redirtied with folio_redirty_for_writepage and the buffer skipped), and a buffer that was dirty is marked for asynchronous write with end_buffer_async_write while a clean one is unlocked. Then writeback is started on the folio, each asynchronous-write buffer is submitted with submit_bh_wbc as a write (flags derived from wbc), and the folio is unlocked. If no buffer was submitted, writeback is ended on the folio immediately; otherwise it ends later through end_buffer_async_write. The function returns 0 in that case. If get_block fails with error err, it takes the recovery path: the mapped, dirty, non-delayed buffers are locked and marked for async write while the other buffers are cleaned, mapping_set_error(folio->mapping, err) is called, writeback is started, the marked buffers are submitted, the folio is unlocked, writeback is ended at once if nothing was submitted, and err is returned. In both cases the folio is unlocked on return; the caller no longer holds the folio lock and the folio is either under writeback with submitted I/O or has had its writeback ended.

name: cachefiles_daemon_bind
prose: Precondition: cache points to a cachefiles_cache holding the configuration set so far (run, cull and stop percentages for files and blocks, rootdirname and tag, which may be NULL) and args points to the NUL-terminated argument string of the bind command. Postcondition: returns -ERANGE, changing nothing, if the file thresholds do not satisfy fstop < fcull < frun < 100 or the block thresholds do not satisfy bstop < bcull < brun < 100; -EINVAL (with a message) if rootdirname is NULL; -EBUSY if CACHEFILES_READY is already set. With CONFIG_CACHEFILES_ONDEMAND enabled, an args string equal to "ondemand" sets CACHEFILES_ONDEMAND_MODE in cache->flags and any other non-empty args returns -EINVAL; without that option any non-empty args returns -EINVAL. If cache->tag is NULL it is set to a kstrdup copy of "CacheFiles" (-ENOMEM if that fails; the tag is deliberately not freed on error because the release handler frees it). Otherwise it returns the result of cachefiles_add_cache(cache), 0 meaning the cache is now bound and ready. On the -EINVAL (args) and -ENOMEM returns the ondemand mode flag may already have been set; no lock is taken or released here.
